title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers used AI-generated video to impersonate a named, real attorney and created thousands of fake social media profiles across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram to advertise fraudulent immigration services. The fabricated videos showed a synthetic likeness of the attorney making specific promises about residency assistance and directing viewers to a WhatsApp contact, where victims were sent phony contracts and asked to pay through peer-to-peer payment apps. This is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated media served as the lure, operating entirely outside any platform or service the real attorney controlled.

The failure point was on the social media platforms themselves, where the volume of fake profiles, nearly 6,500 removed, suggests detection did not happen automatically or quickly. The scheme persisted long enough for an anti-piracy firm hired privately to do the removal work the platforms had not done. Catching it earlier would have required either automated detection of synthetic media at upload or faster response to the identity complaints of the person being impersonated.

What is not established is who the scammers are, whether any victims recovered money, or whether platform policies were violated in ways that will result in any legal consequence.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney, Angel Leal, who has practiced law for over 30 years, reported that criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud immigrants. Scammers created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos featuring Leal offering fraudulent immigration services. In the videos, the digital version of Leal promises US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for $2,200. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, though suspicious activity first appeared in October. The fraud has escalated dramatically over the past three months.

Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically start with social media videos directing viewers to contact a WhatsApp number, then involve exchanging phony contracts and requesting payment through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal warned immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to be suspicious of immediate payment requests. He changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the fraud.
